paper.title: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems
paper.central_claim: MemEvolve, a meta-evolutionary framework that jointly evolves agents' experience and the memory architecture (encode/store/retrieve/manage) via diagnose-and-design under a bilevel loop, improves frameworks such as SmolAgent and Flash-Searcher by up to 17.06% and yields memory architectures that transfer across benchmarks and backbones.

G.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. The bottleneck (a fixed memory architecture across task families) is concrete and shown by the paper's own Table 3: hand-designed memories are unstable and ExpeL is below no-memory on all three. Twelve memory systems are re-implemented. Not 4: the automated agent-design/self-referential lineage (ADAS-type, H21 members) is not discussed.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. The bilevel loop (empty-memory inner runs → three-way fitness → Pareto parent selection → trajectory-replay diagnosis → constrained redesign within the four-module interface) is a reasoned response. Not 4: no prediction distinguishing it from random mutation or design without diagnosis.

X.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. K_max=3, K=1, S=3, 60 trajectories (40 new + 20 reused), empty memory per iteration, the BaseMemoryProvider interface and the frozen deployment can be reconstructed. Not 4: candidate validity checks, rollback, design prompts and lineage rules are missing, and greedy K=1 keeps no non-improving candidates.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with son55. Exact-match and LLM-as-judge protocols are both supported, and which benchmark uses which is not stated. WebWalkerQA is a 170-query sample. The reported GAIA 73.33 has two incompatible provenances (App. 9.1 vs Sec. 5.3/Table 3), a reporting-integrity failure under the run cap (r09b EvoRoute/AgentDevel). The 'up to 17.06 %' headline is an absolute-point gain on the weakest baseline. Cost/latency/steps are reported alongside, and GAIA/WW counts are consistent k/n.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The no-memory control and seven re-implemented human memories on the same framework are informative. There is no evolved-vs-seed (AgentKB-style) number, no diagnose-vs-random redesign and no K/S/round ablation, and re-implementation fidelity is unverified (ExpeL < no-memory everywhere).

E.holdout.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked, with a shared correction. The TaskCraft→WebWalkerQA/xBench transfer and the cross-LLM runs are real separation. GAIA is affected by Level-1 use in evolution or misreported provenance. The TaskCraft column includes the 120 evolution queries (k/300; opus:O01), which both seats left as 'unclear'.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked (A2 ladder). Single-run pass@1, no seeds, intervals or tests; sample sizes and negative baseline results are given.

E.cost.reason: Opus sides with son55. No evolved-vs-seed number, no evolution cost. GAIA provenance conflict; TaskCraft k/300 overlap.
